lines: +# gate.yml — THE gate of a build: drive, fonts, hidden desktop and WebGL, on
+# each leg's native runner. Called by release.yml on the archives it just
+# built and by republish.yml on another run's, and written ONCE for both.
+# Until 2026-10-17 each of the two carried its own copy, and republish's had
+# drifted: no font gate, no `--click` on Windows and arm64, the published core
+# instead of the one from git and no seal, so it could not gate a new engine
+# at all (EngineMismatch), which is exactly when it is needed. Two copies of a
+# gate are two gates, and the one that runs less goes stale first.
+        description: the run whose asset-* artifacts to gate (the caller's own, or another's)
+        description: the tag of the local seal the wrapper's guards run under (the plan's)
+  # DRIVE GATE — the firefox-8 catcher. A raw `firefox --screenshot` proves
+  # nothing about automation: a juggler-less binary renders fine and ships
+  # broken (firefox-8 did exactly that). So we DRIVE every binary the way users
+  # will: Playwright launches it over the juggler pipe, loads a real page, and
+  # round-trips JS. A binary missing/broken juggler throws TargetClosedError
+  # here and the release never publishes. Headless, NO screenshot → GPU-free,
+  # so it can't false-fail on the GPU-less hosted runners. Zero proxy / zero
+  # secrets → safe in public CI (the proxy realness gate stays local, by design).
+  # Each leg runs on its NATIVE runner so we test the real artifact, not a cross
+  # surrogate. Playwright is pinned to a version validated against this build's
+  # juggler; bump it in lockstep when the juggler is re-synced from upstream.
+          # ONE move and ONE click and nothing else; no flag is SMOKE.
+          # ⛔ THE COMMENT THAT STOOD HERE WAS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A DEAD
+          # MOUSE. It said: the interaction code is platform-identical JS (omni.ja),
+          # so one reliable full run catches a firefox-2-class regression for all
+          # platforms. Measured 2026-08-19: a MOZILLA_OFFICIAL build shows the
+          # terms-of-use preonboarding modal, a full-viewport chrome overlay that
+          # swallows EVERY mouse event while the keyboard keeps working - and
+          # `#ifdef XP_LINUX`, so Linux is IMMUNE. The single leg that tested the
+          # mouse was the single leg that could not see the defect: all five legs
+          # green, mouse dead on Windows and macOS - the target platform.
+          # So win and mac now run `--click`. It stays LIGHT on purpose: the
+          # flakiness that made --full linux-only came from a heavy interaction
+          # sequence, not from one click, and this defect class produces ZERO
+          # events rather than wrong ones. See scripts/ci_drive_gate.py.
+          # ⛔ NOT hardcoded to main. The gate validates the BINARY, and the
+          # wrapper is only the instrument it is driven with: unfinished work
+          # on the wrapper's main must not be able to block a binary release.
+          # Default stays main, because main is what gets published next and is
+          # therefore the honest pairing - this is an escape hatch, not a
+          # ⛔ AND THIS IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS THE CORE, which is
+          # installed from git@main a few steps below and must STAY that way:
+          # during a release the published core is one step behind BY
+          # CONSTRUCTION, because its version derives from a seal that cannot
+          # exist until this binary is built. Pinning the core to the index
+          # tests a pairing no user ever gets, and it bit on firefox-20.
+          # another run's artifacts need the token; this run's do not
+      - name: Install Playwright driver (no bundled browser — we override executable_path)
+        # Pin from a SINGLE source (scripts/playwright_pin.txt) so release.yml and
+        # verify-assets.yml can't drift to different versions. The drive gate then
+        # ENFORCES playwright↔juggler compatibility: an incompatible pin fails the
+        # launch/drive (TargetClosedError / protocol error) and nothing publishes.
+        # Bump the pin file in lockstep when the juggler is re-synced from upstream.
+      - name: Linux system deps for headless firefox
+        run: sudo "$(which python)" -m playwright install-deps firefox
+          [ -e "$EXE" ] || { echo "ERROR: firefox binary not found at $EXE"; exit 1; }
+      - name: DRIVE GATE — Playwright launch via juggler + real page (+ interaction on --full)
+      # FONT GATE - assert this leg's binary exposes EXACTLY the Windows font
+      # persona: the SAME family set on every OS (the local Win/Linux parity we
+      # can prove by hand), host-leak 0, and the CSS generics mapping to Windows
+      # fonts. This is the ONLY place macOS/CoreText font handling is validated -
+      # there is no local Mac - so a Mac-only regression (e.g. host fonts leaking
+      # through CoreText, or the bundle-only skip not wired in) fails HERE, on the
+      # real artifact, each architecture on its own CPU, before anything ships.
+      # "Each on its own CPU" is load-bearing and was not true for one release: in
+      # firefox-18 the x86_64 asset was driven under Rosetta, so this gate ran
+      # against a translation layer rather than an Intel machine. It cannot see an
+      # Intel-only fault that way, and it stayed green.
+      # Headless, no proxy, no secrets. See scripts/ci_font_gate.py in the wrapper.
+      - name: FONT GATE - exactly the Windows font persona on this OS
+      # HIDDEN-DESKTOP + WEBGL-MASKING GUARDS - run the wrapper's e2e checks
+      # against THIS leg's freshly-built artifact, on its native runner. The
+      # wrapper's headless=True is headed+hidden: on Windows the browser is
+      # created on a hidden Win32 desktop (since 2026-09-20; until then the
+      # binary cloaked its own window with DWMWA_CLOAK, and this step kept its
+      # name so old runs stay findable), on Linux it gets its own Xvfb. Linux
+      # (Xvfb + llvmpipe) and Windows (WARP) give a software WebGL context on
+      # the GPU-less hosts, so the WebGL-dependent assertions run there.
+      # test_hidden_desktop asserts, on Windows, that a headless=True session
+      # leaves NO Firefox window on the interactive desktop and has one on its
+      # own, after a control arm found a headed window where it belongs, AND
+      # that it still renders; Linux self-skips (Xvfb is the e2e.yml path).
+      # The webgl guard catches a regression of the gamma readPixels noise back to
+      # the pixelscan-maskable ±1 spike form (covered on Linux + Windows).
+      # ⛔ THE CORE COMES FROM GIT, NOT FROM THE INDEX, and this is not a
+      # convenience. `pip install ".[dev]"` installs the WRAPPER, which pins
+      # invisible-core exactly, so pip resolves the PUBLISHED core - and during a
+      # release the published core is always one step behind by construction: its
+      # own version is derived from the seal, so it cannot exist until this binary
+      # has been built and the seal rolled onto it.
+      # That means the pairing this gate used to test - new binary, previous
+      # published core - IS ONE NO USER EVER GETS. A user installing core 19.14.0
+      # downloads the firefox-19 binary, because that is what its seal pins. The
+      # gate was validating an impossible combination.
+      # MEASURED on firefox-20, which is where it finally bit: the binary requires
+      # core emits neither, and StealthDeclarationGate refuses. Not at startup -
+      # a direct headless launch is fine, which is why the first diagnosis went
+      # the wrong way - but on ctx.new_page(), where the browser dies with
+      # exitCode 0x80000003 (a deliberate MOZ_CRASH) and Playwright reports
+      # TargetClosedError. All five legs failed identically in about a minute,
+      # which is the shape of a setup fault and not of five product defects.
+      # Bisected with extra_prefs: either declaration alone is not enough, both
+      # together revive it, and the shader-language pref is not involved.
+      # THE CORE GOES IN FIRST, FROM GIT, AND THE WRAPPER AFTER IT. The core's
+      # version is derived from the seal, not bumped per commit, so git and the
+      # index can both call themselves 19.14.0: installed first, the git core
+      # satisfies the wrapper's exact pin and pip keeps it - same version string,
+      # It used to go the other way (wrapper first, then the core force-
+      # reinstalled with --no-deps), which assumed the version does not move
+      # during a release. firefox-47 broke that: the juggler moved to
+      # modules/juggler, so the core that ships with the binary is a NEW core
+      # (47.x) and the published one (46.x) cannot even find the juggler. With
+      # the old order the wrapper of main kept its 46 pin, the import-time
+      # enforce_core_pin repaired the core back to 46, and every leg failed on a
+      # ⛔ AND THE CORE-FIRST ORDER FAILED TOO, IN THE WRONG PLACE AND SILENTLY
+      # (firefox-51, run 39398286614). It needed a wrapper_ref whose pin names
+      # the version core_ref builds, and during a release that version exists
+      # only on a transition seal: core_ref built 51.48.0, the wrapper of main
+      # pinned 50.48.0, pip put the published core back, and this step PRINTED
+      # "core under test: 50.48.0" and went on. The engine refused the launch on
+      # the two declarations 50.48.0 does not emit (edge_tolerance,
+      # system_quality), and a release build's MOZ_CRASH prints nothing: three
+      # legs red with "the browser exited during startup ... printed:
+      # (nothing)", which reads as a broken binary. A wrapper branch pinned to
+      # 51.48.0 was tried and is not the fix: its own suite runs against the
+      # transition seal, which has no assets, and goes red for that.
+      # SO THE GATE RUNS EXACTLY core_ref, WHATEVER THE WRAPPER PINS. The wrapper
+      # goes in first, for its dependencies; core_ref is force-installed over it
+      # from git, with its own dependencies; and the import-time repair that
+      # broke firefox-47 is switched off for the whole step with the core's own
+      # allow (the pin mismatch warns instead of refusing the import). Then the
+      # core under test is ASSERTED before any browser starts: the git install of
+      # exactly core_ref (direct_url.json, which pip writes for a VCS install and
+      # an index install does not have), read AFTER importing the wrapper, so a
+      # repair that came back any other way is caught here and named.
+      # Measured locally on firefox-51's engine: without the two switches the
+      # repair reinstalls 50.48.0 and the assertion stops the step with that
+      # cause; with them the core stays 51.48.0 and the browser launches and
+      # evaluates with no prefs passed by hand.
+          import json, os, re, subprocess, sys
+              peeled = [s for s, r in rows if r.endswith("^{}")]  # an annotated tag: its commit, not the tag object
+              want = (peeled or [s for s, _ in rows] or [""])[0]
+          import invisible_playwright  # noqa: F401 - the import-time pin repair runs here, as under pytest
+          got = (json.loads(raw).get("vcs_info") or {}).get("commit_id") if raw else None
+          print("core under test: %s from %s" % (version("invisible-core"), got or "the index"))
+          if not want or got != want:
+              sys.exit("THE CORE UNDER TEST IS NOT core_ref: installed %s from %s, core_ref %r is %s. "
+                       "Something put another core over the git install (an install after it, or the wrapper's "
+                       "import-time repair with INVISIBLE_CORE_AUTOFIX not off), and with the published core "
+                       "the engine refuses the launch on the declarations that core does not emit."
+                          want or "not a full sha nor a ref of invisible_core"))
+# publish.yml — the seal and the DRAFT release of a gated build. Called by
+# release.yml (kind=release) on the archives it just built and by
+# republish.yml on another run's, and written ONCE for both: the two copies
+# had already diverged once (republish's produced no seal, 2026-07-25).
+# The payload refusal was republish's alone; on every publish now, it is also
+# what stops the run that publishing a draft re-triggers (the new tag is a
+# `firefox-*` push) from overwriting the published assets with a rebuild.
+        description: the run whose asset-* and source-commit artifacts to publish
+          # ⛔ NOT hardcoded to main. The gate validates the BINARY, and the
+          # wrapper is only the instrument it is driven with: unfinished work
+          # on the wrapper's main must not be able to block a binary release.
+          # Default stays main, because main is what gets published next and is
+          # therefore the honest pairing - this is an escape hatch, not a
+          # ⛔ AND THIS IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS THE CORE, which is
+          # installed from git@main a few steps below and must STAY that way:
+          # during a release the published core is one step behind BY
+          # CONSTRUCTION, because its version derives from a seal that cannot
+          # exist until this binary is built. Pinning the core to the index
+          # tests a pairing no user ever gets, and it bit on firefox-20.
+          # another run's artifacts need the token; this run's do not
+      - name: Assert all 3 target archives present (no silent partial release)
+            [ -s "$a" ] || { echo "ERROR: missing/empty release asset: $a (a build leg silently dropped out?)"; exit 1; }
+          # explicit glob — never include checksums.txt itself (the `*`-includes-itself trap)
+      # The tag, its number for the title and the previous tag for the changelog
+      # range are the caller's plan (scripts/release_plan.py), not derived here.
+          echo "publishing DRAFT release for tag: ${{ inputs.tag }}"
+      - name: Build release notes from the source commits
+          # previous release's recorded source commit — gives the changelog range.
+          # Missing (first automated notes / firefox-0) -> notes omit the changelog.
+            echo "no previous source-commit.txt — changelog section omitted this time"
+          # publish THIS build's source commit so the next release can diff from it
+      - name: Refuse a payload change under an existing tag
+          # cmp against a file that is not there reports "differs", and this step
+          # would then blame a payload change that never happened while the real
+          # fault is upstream. Name the real fault instead.
+            echo "ERROR: dl/seal.json is missing or empty, so there is nothing to compare"
+            echo "the published seal against and nothing to upload. The 'Generate + gate"
+            echo "seal.json' step must run before this one."
+              echo "ERROR: $TAG already has a published seal for a DIFFERENT payload."
+              echo "A new payload gets a new tag. Mint firefox-\$((N+1)) from the same artifacts."
+              diff <(python3 -m json.tool published/seal.json) <(python3 -m json.tool dl/seal.json) || true
+            echo "no seal published under $TAG yet (first seal), proceeding"
+      - name: Create DRAFT release with all assets
+# release.yml — build all 3 patched-Firefox targets (Win + Linux x2) at $0 and publish them as
+# DRAFT GitHub Release assets, named per the wrapper contract (constants.ARCHIVE_NAME).
+# DRAFT on purpose: a human runs the realness gate and only THEN un-drafts + bumps
+# PACKAGING (issue #14: dangling symlinks broke 265 downloads — never again):
+#   Linux → cp -aL (dereference ALL symlinks into real files) + rm dev tools +
+#           strip + sanitize + tar at ROOT, then validate_release.py as a HARD
+#           in-pipeline gate (the exact battle-tested script from the source repo).
+#   Win   → mach package; zip the CONTENTS of dist/firefox (clean tree, NOT
+#           dist/bin) so firefox.exe sits at the zip ROOT.
+# DRIVE GATE (the firefox-8 catcher): after build, every binary is DRIVEN by
+# Playwright on its native runner (launch via juggler + real page + JS roundtrip,
+# headless, no screenshot → GPU-free, zero proxy). A juggler-less binary renders
+# a screenshot fine but is undrivable — only an actual drive catches that. The
+# proxy realness gate (fppro/webrtc) stays LOCAL — it needs secrets.
+# Trigger: push a tag `firefox-N`, or run manually.  Hybrid runners, all free.
+# A run by hand is a CANDIDATE (build + gate, nothing published, a green run)
+# unless it says kind=release; the `plan` job decides, once, before any build
+# (scripts/release_plan.py), and every job reads its outputs.
+          candidate: build and gate, publish nothing (no seal, no draft); its
+          archives stay the run's artifacts, and republish.yml publishes them
+          from its run id. release: also the seal and the DRAFT under
+        description: 'firefox-N to publish the draft under; kind=release only, a candidate refuses one'
+          invisible_playwright ref the gate runs against. Defaults to main,
+          which is what will be published next and therefore the right thing to
+          validate a new binary with. Set it to a published TAG while the
+          wrapper is mid-rewrite: otherwise unfinished work on main blocks a
+          binary release that has nothing to do with it.
+          invisible_core ref the gate installs. Defaults to main, for the reason
+          the gate step gives. Set it to the branch that follows a change of the
+          engine's layout (firefox-47 moved the juggler to modules/juggler):
+          main still reads the old one and refuses every launch. The core is
+          installed before the wrapper, so wrapper_ref must pin the version this
+  # What this run is, decided once and before the builds: a release with a bad
+  # tag is refused here in seconds, not at the seal two hours later, and a
+  # candidate never reaches the seal at all.
+      - name: The plan refuses what it must
+        # ⛔ `host:` NON e' una proprieta' della gamba, e' una proprieta' del
+        # RUNNER: ogni gamba che gira su `ubuntu-24.04` deve dichiarare il
+        # triplet host, o configure si ferma con
+        #     ERROR: Don't know how to translate x86_64-pc-linux-gnu for rustc
+        # L'immagine ubuntu-24.04 di oggi fa riportare al compilatore C
+        # `x86_64-pc-linux-gnu`, e Firefox non sa mappare quel nome su quello
+        # che rustc usa. E' lo stesso sistema: cambia solo come si chiama.
+        # Vale anche per win-x86_64, che si CROSS-COMPILA da quel runner linux:
+        # il suo --target dice dove va, non da dove parte, e a fermarsi e' la
+        # rilevazione dell'HOST. linux-arm64 gira su `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, host
+        # aarch64, che si traduce da solo - infatti e' l'unica delle tre che ha
+        # A firefox-20 non serviva a nessuna: la matrice qui e' identica campo
+        # per campo, a cambiare e' stata l'immagine sotto.
+          # The GH-hosted 14GB-free disk is tight for a full Firefox build: objdir
+          # (.o + libxul) + `mach package` (a second dist copy) + the archive, plus
+          # 16G of swap and, on the win-cross leg, the fetched MSVC toolchain. The
+          # first firefox-18 win leg packaged fine and the second died on
+          # `No space left on device` at packaging time - i.e. marginal, not broken.
+          # Reclaim the big preinstalled caches up front so it stops being marginal.
+          # Everything here is best-effort (|| true) - a missing path must never fail
+          sudo fallocate -l 16G /swapfile && sudo chmod 600 /swapfile && sudo mkswap /swapfile && sudo swapon /swapfile || true
+      # Cheapest gate in the pipeline, guarding the most expensive failure: the asset
+      # basename is hand-written in every matrix entry below and derived independently
+      # on the client side. When the two disagree CI publishes one name while the
+      # wrapper fetches another, so every download 404s while the build is green, the
+      # archives are valid and the release page looks correct (issue #14). Fail here in
+      # seconds instead of after five multi-hour builds.
+      - name: Check asset names match the version this tree builds
+      # Juggler tested without a browser, seconds here before hours of build.
+      # The channel between its two halves: a request answered from another
+      # channel end's kept answers is never dispatched and nothing says so (a
+      # page's "main world created" was lost that way, B286). And where it loads
+      # from: never a chrome package, which a page probes by name, and every
+      # resource URL a file the build installs (invisible_playwright #336).
+      - name: Juggler's tests without a browser
+        # The files, expanded by the shell: from Node 21 the arguments of
+        # --test are file patterns, and a directory is loaded as a module.
+      # The release scripts' own known-bad inputs: validate_release.py's
+      # no-updater and no-juggler-name checks, and make_seal.py's refusals. A
+      # check that has only ever printed its OK line is not a gate.
+      - name: The release scripts refuse what they must
+      # Record which firefox_antidetect_patch commit this build came from. The publish
+      # job turns the range previous-release..this commit into the release notes
+      # (scripts/gen_release_notes.py), and re-publishes it as a source-commit.txt
+      # asset so the NEXT release knows where to start the changelog. One leg is
+      # enough — all legs check out the same SOURCE_REF.
+      - name: Record source commit (for auto release notes)
+        run: git rev-parse HEAD > source-commit.txt && cat source-commit.txt
+      # The page-surface gate at the packaging step asks invisible_core which
+      # engine with the branding redirect (P60) serves that archive, not the
+      # brand in its omni.ja, so that archive is what a page reads and what is
+      # judged. The core is the one the drive gate pairs with the binary,
+      # core_ref, so both gates judge the same pairing. An engine without the
+      # redirect never asks, and the install stays unconditional on purpose:
+      # every engine built from a tree with P60 redirects, so a conditional
+      # would only be a second place deciding what serves_declared_branding
+      # already decides from the tree, and a core_ref that cannot install
+      # fails the drive gate of the same run.
+      # BEFORE the build, and the question asked once here: the core's answer
+      # does not depend on the build. It used to be installed after `mach
+      # build`, so a core whose contract had moved was found at the packaging
+      # step, two hours in: every leg of the first firefox-50 candidate died
+      # there, because core 49.46.0 refuses a profile translated without a
+      # session zone and the gate did not pass one.
+      - name: Install the invisible_core the page-surface gate asks for its branding
+          python3 -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print('core asked for the branding:', version('invisible-core'))"
+          ( cd scripts && python3 -c "import validate_release; print('branding it declares:', validate_release.declared_branding())" )
+          sudo apt-get install -y util-linux binutils ${{ matrix.extra_pkgs }}
+        run: rustup target add ${{ matrix.rust_target }} || true
+      - name: Extend the repo .mozconfig (NO mold; +target/SDK as needed)
+          test -f .mozconfig || { echo "ERROR: no .mozconfig in source"; exit 1; }
+          # VIA sccache SU QUESTI RUNNER, o mach build muore prima di compilare
+          # Il .mozconfig e' UNO SOLO per le due macchine di sviluppo e per la
+          # senza percorso, apposta: il percorso e' una proprieta' della
+          # macchina, e sulle due macchine sccache sta nel PATH. Su un runner
+          # nudo non c'e', e nessuno se n'era accorto perche' release.yml non
+          # girava da firefox-20 mentre la riga e' entrata dopo.
+          # E qui non servirebbe comunque: un runner e' effimero, quindi la
+          # cache nasce VUOTA a ogni corsa, e la prima build con sccache e' piu'
+          # LENTA di una senza perche' deve popolarla. Installarlo sarebbe
+          # pagare un costo per un beneficio che non puo' esistere.
+          # Case-insensitive, perche' c'e' anche SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE maiuscolo.
+          # Solo le righe ATTIVE: i commenti che spiegano il perche' restano.
+            echo "# --- release CI levers for ${{ matrix.leg }} (mold intentionally OFF — it segfaults libxul) ---"
+          if [ -n "${{ matrix.target }}" ]; then echo "ac_add_options --target=${{ matrix.target }}" >> .mozconfig; fi
+          if [ -n "${{ matrix.host }}" ]; then echo "ac_add_options --host=${{ matrix.host }}" >> .mozconfig; fi
+          # No --disable-default-browser-agent here: the .mozconfig dropped it on
+          # 2026-08-19 because the retail release builds the agent (only the
+          # installer registers it, and we ship an archive), and this leg kept
+          # adding it back, so the agent's page-readable image was missing from
+          # every Windows build (B157, found by the page-surface gate).
+            # The C++ runtime ships beside the binaries, as the retail ships it
+            # (B306): windows.configure packages it only under MOZ_AUTOMATION or
+            # with this option, and this cross leg had neither, so a clean
+            # Windows could not start the browser. A toolchain without
+            # Redist/MSVC fails configure at once, loudly.
+        # ⛔ Un tetto sul PASSO, non solo sul job. Il 2026-08-26 la gamba
+        # win-x86_64 si e' piantata sul download del toolchain Microsoft che
+        # `--enable-bootstrap` fa a inizio build: nessuna riga emessa per oltre
+        # tre ore, con il contatore di mach fermo a 0:29. Senza questo tetto la
+        # corsa avrebbe consumato le 6 ore del job prima di arrendersi, e il
+        # guasto si riconosce solo aprendo il log e notando che il contatore non
+        # 180 minuti sono il 48% sopra la piu' lenta build riuscita mai
+        # osservata su questa gamba (121 min il 2026-08-26; 105 e 106 il
+        # 2026-08-17), quindi non uccide una build lenta ma vera. Quando scatta,
+        # il job risulta FALLITO invece che appeso, e `rerun-failed-jobs`
+        # ricompila la sola gamba caduta riusando gli artefatti delle altre.
+      # ── LINUX: dereference symlinks (issue #14) + strip + sanitize + tar@root + GATE
+          # The PACKAGED tree, as the Windows leg ships it (B310). This leg used
+          # to tar obj-rel/dist/bin, the development tree: the test binaries and
+          # TLS test servers went out with it, and the 44 locale .properties a
+          # page can read kept the comments the packager strips, so they differed
+          # from the retail's. A failing `mach package` fails the leg.
+          [ -x "$DIST/firefox" ] || { echo "ERROR: mach package did not produce $DIST/firefox"; exit 1; }
+          cp -aL "$DIST/." "$STAGING/"                      # -L: dereference ALL symlinks into real files
+          [ "$N" -eq 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: $N symlinks remain after cp -aL"; exit 1; }
+          # JUGGLER GATE: present (Playwright cannot drive the binary without it).
+          # PAGE-SURFACE GATE: what a page can read of the build (registered
+          # names and the bytes of every readable file) is the retail's of the
+          # same version, judged against Mozilla's complete MAR (stock_parity.py).
+          # Both live in validate_release.py, which also runs on the archive below.
+          # Every gate runs and reports before the verdict (scripts/release_gates.py).
+          STAGING="$STAGING" python3 scripts/linux_sanitize.py || true   # no-op in CI (no /home/feder), defensive
+          echo "=== HARD GATE: scripts/validate_release.py (the issue-#14 protector) ==="
+          # --no-site-patterns: the site-name token list is deliberately not in this
+          # repository and cannot be on a CI runner, so this leg checks structure and
